text: Ryn gathers Dav, Dell to talk.

speaker: a009
text: Pile's gone and I walked away with nothing again — Dav, you took your two like we agreed, but Vela doubled back and cleaned out what was left before I could move, and now I'm sitting on three food with a year ahead of me and Dell still young enough to need more than I can give alone. I want to know if we're holding to the same plan or if the rules we set last night need to change, because a family that agreed on fair shares shouldn't be the one coming up empty while Vela eats six.

speaker: a005
text: Vela's forty-eight and took six food — that's not hunger, that's hoarding against a death she can feel coming, and I won't let her desperation bleed into you. Ryn, I'm sitting on three right now; take one of mine before the day's out. Dell, the lesson here is that we agreed on fair shares among ourselves, not with the whole village — next year someone needs to move at the pile before Vela gets a second pass.

speaker: a009
text: Dav, I'll take the food — thank you, and I mean it the way you mean that kind of thing when it costs you. Dell, next year you move first, before Vela, before anyone — you're fast and you know the ground, and your mother being hungry again is not a thing I want to name a third time.

speaker: a005
text: Dell, your mother said it right — you moved first this year and it shows, you've got five food and both of us are still standing, so that instinct is already working. Next year we don't leave it to chance: you're at the pile before anyone else takes a second step, and if Vela or anyone else thinks about a second pass, they do it knowing we're watching and counting.

speaker: a009
text: Dell, you've got five food and I've got four now — between us and your father's two that's nine, and I want to hold most of that into next year rather than eat it down, because the year after that I'll be forty-three and the pile won't get more generous. What I want from both of you tonight is a clear picture of where Mako sits, because a man who waited through the whole pile and then took the last two is either very patient or very sure he doesn't need to hurry.

speaker: a011
text: Mako waited because he knew the pile was deep enough — seven food going in, now he's sitting on seven still, and a man that calm when everyone else is scrambling isn't patient, he's confident, which means he thinks he's already got whatever he needs and doesn't have to hurry for anything. That's the part I want to understand before next year: what does he think he has? Because if it's an arrangement with Bram, those two together at eighty-three and fifty-eight in strength with fourteen food between them is a problem we can't solve by just getting to the pile faster.

speaker: a005
text: Mako's seven and Bram's six — that's thirteen food between two strong men, and neither of them has a child or a woman, which means all of that is muscle and stored time with nowhere to go but into a move against someone. I want to talk to Roan before next year, because he's sitting on four, he just had a son with Sela, and Bram already tried to take from him once — a man Bram targeted once is a man who remembers it. If we can bring Roan in without Sela pulling him toward Mako instead, we change the numbers in this village without throwing a single punch.

speaker: a009
text: Roan's the right target and the right reason, but Sela's the hinge — she had Roan's child, which means she's already chosen something, and if she's leaning toward Mako it's because nobody's given her a better offer. Dell, you're the one who was supposed to talk to her last year; tell me what she said, because I don't want Dav walking into that conversation blind.

speaker: a005
text: Dell, answer your mother — what did Sela actually say to you last year, because if that conversation went nowhere I need to know before I walk into it thinking I've got a soft approach already laid.

speaker: a009
text: Dell hasn't answered yet, which tells me either the conversation with Sela went nowhere worth repeating or it went somewhere she hasn't decided how to tell us — Dell, I love you and I need the truth of it, not the version that keeps the peace in this room.

speaker: a005
text: Dell, your mother and I are both watching you right now and we're not moving until you give us something real — Sela had a child with Roan, which means whatever you said or didn't say last year already played out in a direction neither of us planned for, and I need to know if that's because you warned her off us or because she made her own choice before you got to her.
